newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australis cannot explain share movements.
newsitem.headline: Australis cannot explain share movements.

text.p: Pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said on Thursday it could not explain the recent trading in its stock other than press speculation about industry losses.

The company, which had been queried by the Australian Stock Exchange, said it would release its results for the nine months to end-March on May 30. This information would also include subscriber numbers to May 30.
"However, there are no matters of special importance concerning the company about to be announced," it said.

"The company is not aware of or able to offer any explanation for recent trading in the securities of the company other than press speculation concerning the pay tv industry as a whole and concerning recent problems and losses by the company's competitors," Australis said.
Australis, which competes with the Foxtel and Optus Vision operations, two months ago announced a 1996/97 first half loss of A$141.93 million, with accumulated losses of A$535.77 million.
Analysts have estimated that combined losses from all operators total more than A$1 billion.

Analysts also regard Australis as the weak link in the pay-tv chain and the company most likely to fall by the wayside if its owners and competitors reach an agreement on programming and distribution.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper on Thursday referred to industry reports that News Corp Ltd, which is the half owner of Foxtel, and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd were talking about the local pay-tv industry. PBL led a rescue package for Australis last year.

Australis shares were half a cent lower at 15.5 cents at 10.30 a.m. (0030 GMT). The ASX asked the company if it could explain the rise in its share price from a low of 12 cents last Thursday to 16.5 cents on Wednesday.
